results.title: RL — Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) Explained | by Jonathan Hui | Medium
results.content: # RL — Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) Explained. In order not to make bad decisions, we can shrink the trust region if the policy is changing too much. After considering the upper bound of this error, we can guarantee that the calculated optimal policy within the trust region is always better than the old policy. d* below is the KL-divergence between the old and the new policy. With clipped objective, we compute a ratio between the new policy and the old policy:. We construct a new objective function to clip the estimated advantage function if the new policy is far away from the old policy. > Q-learning (with function approximation) fails on many simple problems and is poorly understood, vanilla policy gradient methods have poor data efficiency and robustness; and trust region policy optimization (TRPO) is relatively complicated, and is not compatible with architectures that include noise (such as dropout) or parameter sharing (between the policy and value function, or with auxiliary tasks).
